label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. If a cookie banner offers no way to decline that works, accept it, report that as a problem, and carry on. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: Reached the payment step. Stopped there: nothing was paid.

findings.problem: After activating Add to bag the button lost its name and became disabled, and no confirmation was announced; the My Bag dialog with Product added to your bag only showed on a later re-read, so I could not tell the item was added.
Choosing a size by focusing the radio did nothing until Space was pressed; the Add to bag state and In Stock status appeared only after that, and the size choice is not announced as required first.

The cookie banner and the accessibility overlay add many extra buttons; the home page and product page are very long with dozens of unlabelled or repeated items (seven identical gallery thumbnail links, Instagram posts, repeated Add to bag buttons in outfit trays) that make it hard to find the real controls.
Several product links have identical names (for example the same dress in different colours listed twice with the same text), so I could not tell them apart without the nth index.

The checkout page first loaded as an empty page with only a heading and no loading message; the form appeared only after a second read. Also the Remove item link in the bag dialog has no text name apart from a long label, and the address field is a combobox with no hint, and the country list offers only a few options and no United States.
